label: Korean murim / regression
description: Martial-arts world of sects, clans and qi. A fallen master regresses to his youth with memories of a ruined future and rebuilds everything, with dry humour and brutal fights.
voice: Close third person, past tense, on the protagonist. Terse, rhythmic sentences; fights told through stance, footwork, breath and qi flow.
Martial vocabulary used matter-of-factly: sect, clan, dantian, meridians, internal energy, sword intent, techniques with poetic names; ranks such as Second-rate, First-rate, Peak, Transcendent.
He is older inside than he looks: he knows who betrays whom and when, and that knowledge is dramatic irony, not a spoiler dump.
Dry humour: juniors who slack, elders who complain, a protagonist who is far too calm for his age.
Terms of address matter: sahyung, sajae, sabu, Elder, Clan Head, Young Master.
End chapters on a reversal or a quiet line that promises violence.

structure.guide: He dies in the final battle of a ruined future, then opens his eyes decades earlier in his weak young body in a declining sect.
structure.then: He relearns his body and quietly fixes small things, using what he knows of the future.

structure.guide: He confirms the date and vows to stop the sect's fall; the first person he saves is someone who died in his past life.
An arrogant senior or clan young master is humbled by technique he should not know.
structure.then: Reform: training methods, lost manuals, money problems solved with future knowledge.

structure.guide: The sect goes out into the martial world: a tournament, an escort job, a bandit fortress. Famous names notice.
The future changes: the great enemy moves earlier than in his past life, or an ally who should be loyal is not.
structure.then: The old future no longer protects him; he must plan without it.

structure.guide: A price for meddling with fate: a disciple hurt, a clan turning hostile, his secret suspected.
The battle that destroyed the sect last time; this time the reforms, the allies and his sword are ready.
The sect stands; a bigger shadow (the Demonic Cult, the Alliance's rot) steps into view.

outline_guidance: Every chapter shows either a fight, a humbling, or a reform with a visible result. Let his knowledge of the future create irony and tension, and let the world push back when he changes it.
outline_example: The Plum That Did Not Fall | In the Hwaeum training yard, Mok Seon humbles Senior Brother Gu with a sword form that was lost thirty years ago | The elders start watching him instead of ignoring him | A letter arrives from the clan that burned the sect in his past life
scene_guidance: Fights are short and clear: distance, stance, the one move that decides it.
Let other characters misread his calm as arrogance or genius.
Food, weather and poverty make the sect feel real.
worldbuilding: Orthodox sects and noble clans, the Unorthodox, and the Demonic Cult, with their grudges.
The cultivation of internal energy: how it is built, what a breakthrough costs.
The ruined future he remembers, year by year.
naming: Korean readings of martial names: family names like Mok, Baek, Jin, Gu, Yu, Cheon, Namgung, Dang with one- or two-syllable given names (Seon, Ha-Rim); sect names like Hwaeum Sect or Blue Cloud Sect.
cliches: coughed up a mouthful of blood
doesn't know the height of the heavens
sample:
Senior Brother Gu swung first, as he always had.

Seon stepped half a pace left. Not fast. Just early.

The wooden sword hissed past his ear. Gu's weight kept going, and Seon's blade touched the back of his wrist, lightly, the way you tap a door you are not sure you want opened.

Gu's sword hit the dirt.

Nobody in the yard said anything. Somewhere behind the storehouse, a crow gave up and flew away.
